details: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has reduced its global growth forecast for 2026 to 3.0% from 3.1%, citing ongoing risks from the Middle East war, trade fragmentation, and potential corrections in AI market expectations. Concurrently, the IMF raised its 2026 headline inflation forecast by 0.6 percentage points to 4.7%, noting that energy prices are 25% higher than before the conflict began. This outlook suggests a challenging macroeconomic environment.
title: IMF Trims 2026 Global Growth Outlook to 3%, Boosts Inflation Forecast

details: Minutes from the Federal Reserve's June FOMC meeting indicate significant disagreement among officials regarding the future trajectory of interest rates. While the benchmark rate remained between 3.50%-3.75%, many policymakers expressed concerns that substantial investment in AI and the Middle East conflict could keep inflation elevated, potentially necessitating rate hikes later in the year. Some members even supported an immediate rate increase.
title: Federal Reserve Divided on Rate Hikes Amid Persistent Inflation

details: The European Central Bank (ECB) has begun applying a "climate factor" to corporate bonds used as collateral, introducing additional valuation deductions based on their exposure to climate transition risks. This policy aims to safeguard against potential financial impacts from climate change and will require banks to hold more capital against bonds issued by companies deemed high-polluting. The Bank of England also plans similar measures later in 2026.
title: ECB Applies Climate Factor to Corporate Bonds in Collateral Framework

details: Renewed US-Iran tensions, including US military strikes and the revocation of Iran's oil sales waiver, have significantly elevated geopolitical risks. This led to a surge in oil prices and a "Black Tuesday" sell-off across US equity markets. Bitcoin, reflecting the general risk aversion, retreated to approximately $62,038.49.
title: Geopolitical Tensions Escalate, Bitcoin Drops Amid Risk-Off Shift

details: The US inflation rate, as measured by the trailing 12-month Consumer Price Index, stands at 4.25% as of July 2026, with the May CPI-U increasing 4.2% over the last year. This persistent elevation in inflation, partly fueled by spiking oil prices due to the conflict in Iran, has contributed to an increase in average 30-year fixed mortgage rates, which have edged above 6.5%.
title: US Inflation at 4.25%, Mortgage Rates Climb Above 6.5%
